the development of a systematised semantic space grounded on the sensory-motor capability of the agent, is a key factor to facilitate linguistic composition and behavioural generalisation in artificial agents controlled by dynamcial neural networks.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the co-development of the linguistic and behavioural skills in an embodied agent.
the development of a computational model for the study of the relationship between language and behaviour in a simulated population of artificial agents.
the study of the relationship between the development of compositional semantics and generalisation in the behaviour of agents controlled by dynamically reconfigurable neural networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(a) the agent’s sensory motor capability is a necessary condition for linguistic compositionality and (b) the semantic space, as the agent’s internal representation of the world, is the sufficient condition.
the agent has developed an internal model of the world and of his own behaviour that allows him to access and execute linguistic instructions that were not experienced during training.

the agents have developed a compositional semantics, based on a sensory motor representation of objects and actions, which allows the agent to generalise the meaning of linguistic instructions and to generalise the execution of actions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that a population of agents, controlled by dynamical recurrent neural networks, is able to develop a semantic space that allows the agents to access and execute linguistic instructions not experienced before.

a population of agents, controlled by dynamical recurrent neural networks, can be trained by artificial evolution, to learn to access and execute linguistic instructions, and that this process can result in the development of semantic spaces that facilitate the composition of linguistic instructions, and the generalisation of behavioural skills.
the agent is able to learn the meaning of words and their combinations by experiencing the world, and that it can generalise the acquired semantic knowledge to novel linguistic instructions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of a compositional semantic space is a necessary condition for behavioural generalisation, and that the development of this semantic space is not a mere consequence of training.

, in the absence of explicit semantic knowledge, the agent can develop a compositional semantics by learning the meaning of the linguistic instructions through its own experience and by exploiting the statistical regularities of the environment.

, by means of artificial evolution, we were able to train dynamical neural networks to develop a compositional semantic space, which in turns allows the development of a behavioural generalisation capability.
